Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Chandra Prakash Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ratan Kumar Bhardhwaj, holding brief of Sri Akhilesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 165 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Kalwari, District Basti, during the pendency of trial.
4. As per prosecution story, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu rites on 01.06.2023.
The applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected the deceased to cruelty for demand of Rs. five lacs as dowry and thereby led her to death on 30.06.2024.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by about five days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

6. Learned counsel has next stated that prior to the institution of the FIR, brother-in-law (devar) of the informant Rampreet had given an application at the police station whereby he had stated that his niece has consumed some poisonous material and she has expired, as such her post mortem may be conducted.
7.
Learned counsel has next stated that in the said application dated 01.07.2024, brother-in-law of the informant has not raised any allegations of demand of dowry.
It is next stated that in the inquest report dated 30.06.2024 at 6:10 p.m., brother-in-law of the informant and other family members were present and no FIR was instituted.

8. Learned counsel has next stated that it is true that deceased had consumed some poisonous Teeju vs State Of U.P. on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120162233/
1 material meant for rodents but the applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.
The truth is that the deceased was having an affair with a boy and she used to have regular parlays with him.
The said C.D.R has been annexed with the supplementary affidavit filed today in the Court.
9. Learned counsel has placed reliance on certain photographs which indicate that the deceased was in love with the said boy.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 15.11.2024 and the trial is moving at snail's pace as only one witness has been examined that too on 19.07.2025.
There is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
10. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the deceased has expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant.
The said act of filing such photographs of the victim/deceased that too after her death and tarnishing her image should not be encouraged.
The said act stands deprecated.
11. This Court had called for a report regarding the status of trial and in compliance thereof, a report dated 06.08.2025 has been submitted by the concerned trial court.

The said report indicates that charge could be framed against the applicant on 29.03.2025.
12.
The said act of annexing the photographs of the deceased stands deprecated by this Court also.

However, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record and taking into consideration the fact that only one witness has been examined to date and the FIR is delayed coupled by the fact that there are certain conversations of the deceased with the said boy and even brother-in-law of the informant had made no allegation of demand of dowry in the said application dated 01.07.2024, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Teeju, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

15. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
(Krishan Pahal,J.) September 2, 2025
